units: <cite ref="Sukkah 51b">Succ. 51ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 4a:6">B. Bath. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>סבר למִשְׁעֲיָין בדהבא</he> he (Herod) intended to cover them (the Temple walls) with gold.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 5:10">Targ. Ps. V, 10</cite> <he>מְשַׁעֲיִין</he>. Ms. (ed. <he>משעעין</he>).—Part. pass. <he>מְשָׁעָא</he>.
Targ. Y. II, Num. XIX, 15 מִשְׁעָא (corr. acc., or מַשְׁעָא, Part. pass. Af.).

senses.gloss: [to make one’s self pleasant,] to converse, talk; to tell a story.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 6:13">Targ. Jud. VI, 13</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 30:10">Targ. Is. XXX, 10</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 50:16">Targ. Ps. L, 16</cite>; <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 50:19">19</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 73a:8">B. Bath. 73ᵃ</cite> <he>אִשְׁתָּעוּ לי נחותי וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="U01653"><he>אשתעי</he></cite>) seafarers told me.

Ib. 74ᵃ ר׳ יוחנן מִשְׁתָּעֵי וכ׳ R. J. told a story: once upon a time &c. Y. Ber. II, 4ᵈ bot. כמה דאי׳ … אִשְׁתָּעְיָיא וכ׳ as the Scripture talks, so does the Mishnah, i.e. the Mishnah applies the Biblical phraseology; a. fr.—א׳ דינא בהדי to talk about the law with, to sue.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 14a:10">B. Mets. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>דינא … ומשתעי דינא בהדיה</he> the law is that R. may go and sue him.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 47b:2">Bekh. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>גברא דלא מצית לאִשְׁתָּעוּיֵי וכ׳</he> a man with whom thou canst not go to law; a. e.
